lab_questions.title: Practical SQLite Evaluation: E-Commerce Order Management
lab_questions.description: Evaluate candidates on practical SQL skills using a realistic e-commerce database. Tasks cover multi-table JOINs with aggregation and HAVING, subqueries/NOT EXISTS filtering for un-ordered products, and top-N revenue analysis.

tasks.title: Task 1: Customers with Multiple Completed Orders
tasks.description: Write a query to find all customers who have placed at least 2 'Completed' orders. Return customer full name (first_name || ' ' || last_name) as customer_name, total number of completed orders as completed_orders, and total amount spent as total_spent. Sort by total_spent descending, then customer_name ascending.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'Completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2 ORDER BY total_spent DESC, customer_name ASC;

solution.task1.sql: SELECT c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS customer_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'Completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2 ORDER BY total_spent DESC, customer_name ASC;

tasks.title: Task 2: Products Never Included in Completed Orders
tasks.description: Write a query to find all products that have never been included in any 'Completed' order (including products never ordered at all or only ordered in Pending, Processing, or Cancelled status). Return product_id, product_name, and category_name. Sort by product_id ascending.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, c.category_name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND o.status = 'Completed') ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;

solution.task2.sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, c.category_name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id AND o.status = 'Completed') ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;

tasks.title: Task 3: Top 5 Best-Selling Products by Revenue
tasks.description: Write a query to determine the top 5 best-selling products based on total revenue generated from 'Completed' orders. Return product_name, category_name, total_quantity_sold, and total_revenue. Sort by total_revenue descending, then product_name ascending. Limit to 5 records.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT p.product_name, cat.category_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN categories cat ON p.category_id = cat.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'Completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, cat.category_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, p.product_name ASC LIMIT 5;

solution.task3.sql: SELECT p.product_name, cat.category_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN categories cat ON p.category_id = cat.category_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'Completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, cat.category_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, p.product_name ASC LIMIT 5;

lab_questions.title: College Academic Analytics
lab_questions.description: A university wants to analyze student academic performance, course enrollment, and departmental performance. The PostgreSQL database has already been configured and populated with realistic data. Write SQL queries to generate three reports for the university administration.

tasks.title: Task 1: Student Performance Report
tasks.description:
The university wants to identify high-performing students.

Write a SQL query that returns students whose average marks across their completed courses are greater than 75.

Return exactly:
- `student_id`
- `student_name`
- `department_name`
- `courses_completed`
- `average_marks`

Requirements:
1. Consider only enrollments with status `completed`.
2. Calculate the average using `marks`.
3. Students must have completed at least 3 courses.
4. Include only students whose average marks are greater than 75.
5. Join the department information.
6. Sort by `average_marks` descending.
7. If averages are equal, sort by `student_id` ascending.
8. Return each student only once.

scoring_rules.system_query: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, d.department_name, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS courses_completed, ROUND(AVG(e.marks), 2) AS average_marks FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.department_id = d.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id WHERE e.status = 'completed' GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, d.department_name HAVING COUNT(e.enrollment_id) >= 3 AND AVG(e.marks) > 75 ORDER BY average_marks DESC, s.student_id ASC;

solution.task1.sql: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name, d.department_name, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS courses_completed, ROUND(AVG(e.marks), 2) AS average_marks FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.department_id = d.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id WHERE e.status = 'completed' GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name, d.department_name HAVING COUNT(e.enrollment_id) >= 3 AND AVG(e.marks) > 75 ORDER BY average_marks DESC, s.student_id ASC;

tasks.title: Task 2: Top Student in Each Department
tasks.description:
The university administration wants to identify the highest-performing students in every department.

Calculate each student's average marks using only completed enrollments and return the top-ranked student(s) in each department.
If multiple students have exactly the same highest average in a department, include all tied students.

Return exactly:
- `department_name`
- `student_id`
- `student_name`
- `average_marks`
- `rank`

Requirements:
1. Consider only `completed` enrollments.
2. Calculate each student's average marks.
3. Rank students separately within each department using a PostgreSQL window function like `RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...)`.
4. Include all students with rank `1`.
5. Sort by `department_name` ascending and `student_id` ascending.

scoring_rules.system_query: WITH student_dept_avg AS (SELECT d.department_name, s.student_id, s.student_name, ROUND(AVG(e.marks), 2) AS average_marks, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY d.department_name ORDER BY AVG(e.marks) DESC) AS rank FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.department_id = d.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id WHERE e.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.department_name, s.student_id, s.student_name) SELECT department_name, student_id, student_name, average_marks, rank FROM student_dept_avg WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY department_name ASC, student_id ASC;

solution.task2.sql: WITH student_dept_avg AS (SELECT d.department_name, s.student_id, s.student_name, ROUND(AVG(e.marks), 2) AS average_marks, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY d.department_name ORDER BY AVG(e.marks) DESC) AS rank FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.department_id = d.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id WHERE e.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.department_name, s.student_id, s.student_name) SELECT department_name, student_id, student_name, average_marks, rank FROM student_dept_avg WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY department_name ASC, student_id ASC;

tasks.title: Task 3: Course Enrollment Analysis
tasks.description:
The university wants to identify courses that have higher-than-average student enrollment.

Write a SQL query that returns courses whose enrollment count is greater than the overall average enrollment across all courses.
Only `active` and `completed` enrollments should be counted.

Return exactly:
- `course_id`
- `course_name`
- `department_name`
- `enrollment_count`
- `average_course_enrollment`

Requirements:
1. Count only enrollments with status `active` or `completed`.
2. Calculate enrollment count separately for each course.
3. Calculate the overall average enrollment across all courses.
4. Return only courses whose enrollment count is greater than the overall average.
5. Include department name.
6. `average_course_enrollment` should represent the overall average used for comparison.
7. Sort by `enrollment_count` descending.
8. If enrollment counts are equal, sort by `course_id` ascending.

scoring_rules.system_query: WITH course_counts AS (SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, d.department_name, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS enrollment_count FROM courses c JOIN departments d ON c.department_id = d.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id WHERE e.status IN ('active', 'completed') GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name, d.department_name), overall_avg AS (SELECT ROUND(AVG(enrollment_count), 2) AS avg_enrollment FROM course_counts) SELECT cc.course_id, cc.course_name, cc.department_name, cc.enrollment_count, oa.avg_enrollment AS average_course_enrollment FROM course_counts cc CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE cc.enrollment_count > oa.avg_enrollment ORDER BY cc.enrollment_count DESC, cc.course_id ASC;

solution.task3.sql: WITH course_counts AS (SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, d.department_name, COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS enrollment_count FROM courses c JOIN departments d ON c.department_id = d.department_id JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id WHERE e.status IN ('active', 'completed') GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name, d.department_name), overall_avg AS (SELECT ROUND(AVG(enrollment_count), 2) AS avg_enrollment FROM course_counts) SELECT cc.course_id, cc.course_name, cc.department_name, cc.enrollment_count, oa.avg_enrollment AS average_course_enrollment FROM course_counts cc CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE cc.enrollment_count > oa.avg_enrollment ORDER BY cc.enrollment_count DESC, cc.course_id ASC;
